LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.1: Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we greet one another? 2. How does pronunciation affect fluency?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to pronounce sounds and words from a given display,

2. collaborate with peers to articulate sounds using Arabic signs (harakat), e.g. fatha, kasra, dhama, sukun

3. listen to Arabic greetings and basic introductions from a recording,

4. work jointly to pick out phrases used in greetings and introduction e.g. good morning, good afternoon, good evening.

5. collaborate with peers to role play a greeting and introduction session to introduce themselves and peers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to pronounce sounds and words from a given display,
2. collaborate with peers to articulate sounds using Arabic signs (harakat), e.g. fatha, kasra, dhama, sukun
3. listen to Arabic greetings and basic introductions from a recording,
4. work jointly to pick out phrases used in greetings and introduction e.g. good morning, good afternoon, good evening.
5. collaborate with peers to role play a greeting and introduction session to introduce themselves and peers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively with peers to pronounce words from a

given display.

• Creativity and imagination: This is promoted as the learner embraces creative ideas when role playing a greetings and

introductions session to introduce themselves and peers.

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates input from peers when picking out phrases used in greetings and

introduction from a recording.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness: This is addressed as the learner interacts with peers when introducing themselves and others as well as

sharing greetings appropriately.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept on greetings and introductions to similar concepts in English and Kiswahili.
